scope: Proposition 5.10 (The central determinant formula) of the manuscript “A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion” (preprints/A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 004 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 df42f33f68fbef77), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose the product L(E(h) , s)L(E(hk) , s) has a simple zero at s = 1. Use the primitive Heegner sum Ph and its free-line index jh defined at the start of Section 4, and put s(h) = lengthZ2 Sha(E(h) /Q)[2∞ ]. Use the primitive Selmer determinant coordinate uh with the fixed class multiplier of Lemma 5.2. For the primitive Selmer diagrams constructed above, we have v(uh(0)) = 2jh − lengthZ2 Sha(E(h) /K)[2∞ ] − 2 ∑︂ p|h tp + OE(1) = 2jh − s(h) − s(hk) − 4w(h) + OE,A(1), ω(k) ≤ A. (5.22) The first error includes the auxiliary prime and the fixed parametrization multiplier. The second has no dependence on the number of primes dividing h.
